messages.body_plain:
On Thu, Mar 7, 2019 at 1:17 AM Emília Wendt <wend...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hello guys
>
> I'm running an analysis with only DEC and DIVA, without the J parameter, and inserting different dispertion matrices, with three time periods.
> Could someone tell me if the number of parameters changes in this case? Or do I still have only 2 parameters (d and e)?
>
> If you change, how should I proceed?
>
>
> Thanks
> --
> Emília W. Wendt
> Mestre em Biologia Animal- UFRGS
> PhD Student - UFRGS
>

Hi -- DEC etc. have 2 parameters. Adding "+J" adds a 3rd parameter.  Different dispersal multiplier matrices or distance matrices are not adding parameters, they are adding fixed changes to models, because:

"parameter" = "free parameter" = something free to change during the ML optimization process, so the value of the parameter is "learned" from the data

If you put, say, +x on a distance matrix, then you are adding another free parameter, because x can vary and be learned from the data during ML.

If you were to use, say, hundreds of different dispersal multiplier matrices and pick the best-fitting one, then that would be equivalent to adding a bunch of free parameters, but I don't think anyone has ever attempted that.

Re: DIVA: Note that I call it "DIVALIKE", as the BioGeoBEARS DIVALIKE it is not identical to Ronquist's 1997 method "DIVA" which used parsimony, ignored branchlengths, etc.  As the script says:

#######################################################
#######################################################
# DIVALIKE AND DIVALIKE+J ANALYSIS
#######################################################
#######################################################
# NOTE: The BioGeoBEARS "DIVALIKE" model is not identical with
# Ronquist (1997)'s parsimony DIVA. It is a likelihood
# interpretation of DIVA, constructed by modelling DIVA's
# processes the way DEC does, but only allowing the
# processes DIVA allows (widespread vicariance: yes; subset
# sympatry: no; see Ronquist & Sanmartin 2011, Figure 4).
#
# DIVALIKE is a likelihood interpretation of parsimony
# DIVA, and it is "like DIVA" -- similar to, but not
# identical to, parsimony DIVA.
#
# I thus now call the model "DIVALIKE", and you should also. ;-)
#######################################################
#######################################################

Ditto for BAYAREALIKE.

Cheers,
Nick

messages.body_plain:
Hi, not sure what this is. "vectors of negative length are not allowed" is not a BioGeoBEARS error message, it is coming from base R or from the operating system. Googling it suggests:

https://www.google.com/search?q=%22%22vectors+of+negative+length+are+not+allowed%22&oq=%22%22vectors+of+negative+length+are+not+allowed%22&aqs=chrome..69i57.1079j0j7&sourceid=chrome&ie=UTF-8

...that it is some problem with memory allocation.  My best guess is:

1. The Biogeographic Stochastic Mapping algorithm actually doesn't use force_sparse at the moment, this hasn't been programmed (and force_sparse is still a bit experimental, sparse matrix exponentiation (faster for huge matrices) seems to be a bit less stable than standard (slow) dense matrix exponentiation, so it is good to check sparse matrix results against standard dense results.

2. To make the BSM simulations fast-ish, what BSM does is store the dense P matrix for each branch (the P matrix is the result of exponentiating the Q transition matrix).

3. For large trees and/or large matrices, step #2 could take a lot of memory, and eventually fill up memory and lead to a crash like you got.

There is a change I could program the sparse stuff into BSM, but in the immediate future I have a lot of other stuff on my plate.  The main solution then would be to try to shrink your state space and ask if you really need all those states.

Cheers!
Nick

messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I'm having a very basic problem with installing BioGeoBEARS, and I hope somebody can point me in the right direction.

I'm trying to install BioGeoBEARS using the example code on the website. See below:

SIMPLE BIOGEOBEARS SETUP
======================================================
# Install optimx
install.packages("optimx", dependencies=TRUE, repos="http://cran.rstudio.com")

# Also get snow (for parallel processing)
install.packages("snow")
library(snow)

# Install phylobase
install.packages("phylobase", dependencies=TRUE, repos="http://cran.rstudio.com")

# Install BioGeoBEARS from CRAN 0-cloud:
install.packages("BioGeoBEARS", dependencies=TRUE, repos="http://cran.rstudio.com")
======================================================

And:

STEP-BY-STEP INSTALLATION OF DEPENDENCIES FOR BIOGEOBEARS
======================================================
# Install optimx
install.packages("optimx", dependencies=TRUE, repos="http://cran.rstudio.com")

# Also get snow (for parallel processing)
install.packages("snow")
library(snow)

# Install BioGeoBEARS from CRAN 0-cloud:
install.packages("BioGeoBEARS", dependencies=TRUE, repos="http://cran.rstudio.com")

# If default install for BioGeoBEARS doesn't work, install dependencies in this order,
# then install BioGeoBEARS from source:
install.packages("Rcpp", dependencies=TRUE)
install.packages("RcppArmadillo", dependencies=TRUE)
install.packages("gdata", dependencies=TRUE)
install.packages("gtools", dependencies=TRUE)
install.packages("xtable", dependencies=TRUE)
install.packages("plotrix", dependencies=TRUE)
install.packages("vegan", dependencies=TRUE)
install.packages("FD", dependencies=TRUE)
install.packages("SparseM", dependencies=TRUE)
install.packages("ape", dependencies=TRUE)
install.packages("phylobase", dependencies=TRUE)
install.packages("rexpokit", dependencies=TRUE)
install.packages("cladoRcpp", dependencies=TRUE)
install.packages("BioGeoBEARS", type="source", dependencies=TRUE, repos="http://cran.rstudio.com")
==============================================

All packages install fine, except BioGeoBEARS itself. I'm constantly getting the error:
"Warning in install.packages :
  package ‘BioGeoBEARS’ is not available (for R version 3.5.0)"

Thinking this was a problem with the R-version that I used, I also tried R versions 3.5.0, 3.5.2 and 3.4.3, and updating Bioconductor, without success. Please note that I used BioGeoBEARS successfully with R v3.4.3, just two months ago. The problems started after I updated to R v3.5.0.

Does anyone have any idea what might be going wrong?

Many thanks already.

All the best,
Eve

messages.body_plain:
Hi Frank et al.,

1. I believe I've fixed this error with area_allowed in BSM one -- the error involved the case where the areas_allowed matrices through time created states_lists for each time bin, but when all of the states_lists for all time-bins were put together, the full list still did not equal the full list of states calculated based on the input areas list and the maxareas argument. (E.g., in these inputs, all of the areas_allowed matrices were the same.)

In general, as I have mentioned before, areas_allowed and areas_adjacency matrices are a crude way to control how the states_list changes by time-period, really it's only appropriate for simple situations like island-disappearance-back-in-time, like Hawaii:

http://phylo.wikidot.com/biogeobears#areas_allowed_matrix2
http://phylo.wikidot.com/biogeobears#better_than_adjacency

 For more complex situations, manually specify your states_lists by time-bin:

Manual modification of states_list (list of geographic ranges, a.k.a. the list of states in the state space)
http://phylo.wikidot.com/example-biogeobears-scripts#manual_modify_states

Re-using the manually modified of states_list
http://phylo.wikidot.com/example-biogeobears-scripts#reuse_modified_states

Manually modify the states list in time-stratified analyses
http://phylo.wikidot.com/example-biogeobears-scripts#modified_states_stratified

2. I also added an error check for BSM if the input areanames are not single-letter codes.

3. Re-install from GitHub to get the fixes.

4. Frank's files attached with minor changes, "NJM" for the ones that aren't e.g. working directory etc.

Cheers!
Nick
